impacts.description: Support for EU biodiversity and climate objectives through policy-relevant ecosystem assessment, protection, restoration planning and biodiversity trend prediction.
Progress toward the goals of the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030 and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, including assessment of progress against their defined targets.
Biodiversity preservation becomes a mainstream feature of other sectors, such as agriculture, transport, energy and the bioeconomy, enabled by FAIR data on species and ecosystems.
Improved knowledge on the status and trends of habitats, species and ecosystems, and on the drivers of decline, built on systemic, harmonised or standardised biodiversity data.

Enhanced AI, machine learning and statistical applications for habitat classification, ecosystem mapping and biodiversity trend prediction, drawing on improved in-situ training and validation datasets.
impacts.inference_note: Derived from expected outcome EO-03, which states that in-situ datasets support AI-based applications for habitat classification, ecosystem mapping and biodiversity trend prediction. The technological impact is the downstream consequence of that stated outcome, not a separately asserted call claim.
